flags.summary: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to begin querying from. This date is inclusive.

flags.name: to_date

flags.name: length
flags.summary: The number of units (defined by length_unit) each user has to complete the funnel, starting from the time they triggered the first step in the funnel. May not be greater than 90 days. Note that we will query for events past the end of to_date to look for funnel completions. This defaults to the value that was previously saved in the UI for this funnel.

flags.name: length_unit
flags.summary: The unit applied to the length parameter can be "second", "minute", "hour", or "day". Defaults to the value that was previously saved in the UI for this funnel.

flags.name: interval
flags.summary: The number of days you want each bucket to contain. The default value is 1.

flags.name: unit
flags.summary: This is an alternate way of specifying interval and can be "day", "week", or "month".

flags.name: on
flags.summary: The property expression to segment the event on. See the [expression to segment](/reference/segmentation-expressions) below.

flags.name: where
flags.summary: An expression to filter events by. See the [expression to segment](/reference/segmentation-expressions) below.

flags.name: limit
flags.summary: Return the top property values. Defaults to 255 if not explicitly included. Maximum value 10,000. This parameter does nothing if \"on\" is not specified.

flags.summary: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to begin querying from. This date is inclusive.

flags.name: to_date
flags.summary: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to query to. This date is inclusive.

flags.name: retention_type
flags.summary: Must be either "birth" or "compounded". Defaults to "birth". The âbirthâ retention type corresponds to first time retention. The âcompoundedâ retention type corresponds to recurring retention. See the [Types of Retention](https://help.mixpanel.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001370146) article for more information.

flags.name: born_event
flags.summary: The first event a user must do to be counted in a birth retention cohort. Required when retention_type is "birth"; ignored otherwise.

flags.name: event
flags.summary: The event to generate returning counts for. Applies to both birth and compounded retention. If not specified, we look across all events.

flags.name: born_where
flags.summary: An expression to filter born_events by. See the [expressions section](/reference/segmentation-expressions) above.

flags.name: where
flags.summary: An expression to filter born_events by. See the [expressions section](/reference/segmentation-expressions) above.

flags.name: interval
flags.summary: The number of units (can be specified in either days, weeks, or months) that you want per individual bucketed interval. May not be greater than 90 days if days is the specified unit. The default value is 1.

flags.name: interval_count
flags.summary: The number of individual buckets, or intervals, that are returned; defaults to 1. Note that we include a "0th" interval for events that take place less than one interval after the initial event.

flags.name: unit
flags.summary: The interval unit. It can be "day", "week", or "month". Default is "day".

flags.name: unbounded_retention
flags.summary: A counting method for retention queries where retention values accumulate from right to left, i.e. day N is equal to users who retained on day N and any day after. The default value of false does not perform this accumulation. [Learn more about Counting Method](https://help.mixpanel.com/hc/en-us/articles/360045484191).

flags.name: on
flags.summary: The property expression to segment the second event on. See the [expressions section](/reference/segmentation-expressions) above.

flags.name: limit
flags.summary: Return the top limit segmentation values. This parameter does nothing if "on" is not specified.

flags.name: project_id
flags.summary: Required if using service account to authenticate request.

flags.name: workspace_id
flags.summary: The id of the workspace if applicable.

flags.name: event
flags.summary: The event that you wish to get data for. Note: this is a single event name, not an array.

flags.name: from_date
flags.summary: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to begin querying from. This date is inclusive.

flags.name: to_date
flags.summary: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to query to. This date is inclusive.

flags.name: on
flags.summary: The property expression to segment the event on. See the [expression to segment](/reference/segmentation-expressions) below.

flags.name: unit
flags.summary: This can be "minute", "hour", "day", or "month". This determines the buckets into which the property values that you segment on are placed. The default value is "day".

flags.name: interval
flags.summary: Optional parameter in lieu of 'unit' when 'type' is not 'general'. Determines the number of days your results are bucketed into can be used with or without 'from_date' and 'to_date' parameters.

flags.name: where
flags.summary: An expression to filter events by. See the [expression to segment](/reference/segmentation-expressions) below.

flags.name: limit
flags.summary: Return the top property values. Defaults to 60. Maximum value 10,000. This parameter does nothing if "on" is not specified.

flags.name: type
flags.summary: This can be "general", "unique", or "average". If this is set to "unique", we return the unique count of events or property values. If set to "general", we return the total, including repeats. If set to "average", we return the average count. The default value is "general".

flags.name: format
flags.summary: Can be set to "csv".

flags.summary: The event or events that you wish to get data for, encoded as a JSON array. Example format: "["play song", "log in", "add playlist"]".

flags.summary: The analysis type you would like to get data for - such as general, unique, or average events. Valid values: "general", "unique", or "average".

flags.name: unit
flags.summary: This can be "minute", "hour", "day", "week", or "month". It determines the level of granularity of the data you get back. Note that you cannot get hourly uniques.

flags.name: interval
flags.summary: The number of "units" to return data for - minutes, hours, days, weeks, or months. 1 will return data for the current unit (minute, hour, day, week or month). 2 will return the current and previous units, and so on. Specify either interval or from_date and to_date.

flags.name: to_date
flags.summary: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to query to. This date is inclusive.

flags.name: format
flags.summary: The data return format, such as JSON or CSV. Options: "json" (default), "csv".
